description: Automated rotation of local administrator account passwords on Windows endpoints. LAPS generates unique, randomly-generated passwords per machine and stores them in Active Directory with ACL-protected access. Prevents lateral movement attacks that rely on shared or default local admin credentials by ensuring each machine has a cryptographically random password that rotates on a defined schedule.

cvss_vector_impacts.rationale: Credential theft yields only single-machine access; password unique per endpoint and rotated
Limits privilege escalation from compromised admin hash; cannot reuse across machines
Lateral movement prevented; compromised local admin cannot authenticate to other systems

verification.method: Verify LAPS policy enforcement and password storage in AD

commands.command: Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name AdmPwdEnabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty AdmPwdEnabled
Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft Services\AdmPwd' -Name PasswordComplexity -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty PasswordComplexity

relationships.rationale: LAPS directly prevents use of default credentials by enforcing unique, auto-generated passwords per endpoint
Eliminates hardcoded/embedded credentials by rotating passwords automatically
Enforces strong password requirements (complexity, length, randomness)

framework_bindings.rationale: Password unique per machine, rotated on schedule
Privilege escalation limited to single endpoint
Lateral movement blocked by unique credentials
LAPS is explicitly mentioned as ATT&CK mitigation M1015
